# `schema-incompatible`

The schema is neither a subset nor a superset

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `error` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `schema-incompatible` (both directions), `schema-incompatible-in-request`, `schema-incompatible-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Core variance rules (fallbacks) ([RULES.md section 1](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

Fallback for a schema change where the new schema is neither a subset nor a superset of the old one (e.g. `string` became `integer`).

## Why this default

Some old values become invalid and some new values are unfamiliar, so clients break in either direction.

## Example

From test case [`schema-incompatible`](../../test/cases/schema-incompatible/): contentMediaType changed: old and new values differ in both directions.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          data:
            type: string
-           contentMediaType: image/png
+           contentMediaType: image/jpeg
```

Findings:

- `schema-incompatible-in-response` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  schema-incompatible: error
```

## How to fix

Add a new field or operation with the new schema instead of changing the existing one.
